payload.goal: Reconcile the attached bank statement CSV against open customer and supplier invoices in Tripletex, matching incoming and outgoing payments and handling partial payments correctly.
success_checks: All bank statement lines from the CSV are imported or represented in reconciliation workflow.
Incoming payments for invoice 1001, 1002, 1003, 1004 and 1005 are matched to the correct customer invoices.
Outgoing payments to Rodrigues Lda, Costa Lda and Almeida Lda are matched to the correct supplier invoices if corresponding open supplier invoices exist.
Partial payments are registered without overpaying or fully closing invoices unless the paid amount equals the open amount.
Unmatched transactions such as Skattetrekk are left as unreconciled or posted to appropriate ledger handling flow.
Bank balance movement in Tripletex reflects the imported statement lines.
risk_notes: Sandbox is empty, so no existing invoices, customers, suppliers or bank account can be assumed.
CSV contains bank transactions but not the actual open invoice register from Tripletex; matching may fail if invoices are missing.
Supplier invoice numbers are not stated for Rodrigues Lda, Costa Lda and Almeida Lda outgoing payments.
Skattetrekk entries are not clearly customer or supplier invoice payments and may require separate voucher handling.
Negative amounts in the Ut column may need normalization depending on import/reconciliation endpoint expectations.
Partial payment handling requires current open balance per invoice, which is not provided in the prompt.
payload.suggested_first_action: Create or configure the bank account and import the CSV statement lines for reconciliation.

ordered_steps: Create or verify bank account in Tripletex for reconciliation context.
Import or parse the CSV statement lines into a reconciliation-ready structure.
Bootstrap missing customers: create Oliveira Lda, Santos Lda and Almeida Lda if absent.
Bootstrap missing suppliers: create Rodrigues Lda, Costa Lda and Almeida Lda as supplier if absent.
Fetch open customer invoices from Tripletex and locate invoice numbers 1001, 1002, 1003, 1004 and 1005.
If customer invoices are missing in empty sandbox, create customer invoices/orders needed so payment matching can be tested.
Fetch open supplier invoices from Tripletex for Rodrigues Lda, Costa Lda and Almeida Lda.
If supplier invoices are missing in empty sandbox, register supplier invoices matching the outgoing payment candidates.
For each incoming bank line, match by invoice reference in text and customer name, then register payment on the corresponding customer invoice with the bank transaction date.
For each outgoing bank line, match by supplier name and open amount, then register payment on the corresponding supplier invoice with the bank transaction date.
Where bank amount is less than invoice open amount, register partial payment and keep residual balance open.
Where multiple open invoices could match a supplier payment, stop for disambiguation or use exact amount/date/reference if available.
Mark Skattetrekk lines as unmatched for invoice reconciliation and route them to separate voucher/ledger review if required.
Finalize reconciliation status and verify all matched transactions are posted correctly.

Do NOT send a JSON body — send empty body or no body. ALL data goes in the URL query string.

paidAmount is the full payment amount (e.g., 47200). For foreign currency, use paidAmountCurrency instead.

Postings with vatType={"id":0} (exempt) can include both debit and credit lines manually.

payload.question: Need minimal-call, zero-4xx execution plan for this bank reconciliation task in an effectively empty sandbox. We must: 1) configure bank account 1920, 2) create 3 customers and 3 suppliers, 3) create products for invoice refs 1001-1005 because orderlines require product ids, 4) create 5 customer orders/orderlines/invoices and register payments on exact transaction dates/amounts, 5) register 3 supplier invoices/payments using POST /ledger/voucher since supplier invoice endpoints are unavailable, and 6) leave 3 Skattetrekk lines unmatched. Please confirm exact required fields and recommended bodies for POST /product, POST /order, POST /order/orderline, POST /invoice, GET /invoice/paymentType, PUT /invoice/{id}/:payment, and POST /ledger/voucher for supplier invoice vouchers in this scenario. Also confirm whether supplier payment matching can be represented at all without a supplier payment endpoint, or if only supplier invoice registration is possible and outgoing bank lines must be reported as not fully reconcilable.

payload.headline: Bank reconciliation failed completely: wrong approach using orders/invoices instead of bank reconciliation API
what_went_wrong: Agent created new customer invoices via orders instead of using the bank reconciliation endpoint (/bank/reconciliation or /bank/statement), which is the correct approach for this task.
Agent never actually reconciled bank statement lines against existing open invoices — it bootstrapped fake invoices and tried to mark them as paid, scoring 0/2 checks.
The supplier payments (Rodrigues Lda, Costa Lda) were never reconciled at all; agent admitted it couldn't find a suitable endpoint for outgoing payments.
5 unnecessary POST /order calls and 5 POST /invoice calls were made to create fake invoices instead of fetching and matching real open invoices.
what_worked: Customers and suppliers were successfully created (Oliveira Lda, Santos Lda, Almeida Lda, Rodrigues Lda, Costa Lda).
Bank account 1920 was configured with isBankAccount=true successfully.
what_to_try_next: Use /bank/reconciliation and /bank/statement endpoints to import the CSV and match bank statement lines to existing open invoices rather than creating new ones.
First fetch existing open customer invoices (GET /invoice?invoiceStatus=OPEN) and supplier invoices (GET /supplierInvoice?status=OPEN) before creating any new entities.
For partial payments, use the payment amount parameter in PUT /invoice/{id}/:payment with the actual partial amount from the bank statement CSV line.
unnecessary_calls: POST /order (x5) — orders should not be created; existing open invoices should be fetched and matched instead.
POST /invoice (x5) — fake invoices created instead of reconciling against real open invoices.
POST /product/list — creating products is irrelevant to bank reconciliation task.
